slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay's country table (the author's AI-assisted compilation) states, citing WHO's 2015 eHealth profile, that there was no EMR or EHR at primary level and that primary care relied on paper forms.

The essay's country table (the author's AI-assisted compilation) states, citing a government audit, that digital systems such as IPCS failed at Area Health Centres, Medi-Clinics and Community Health Centres, with hardware unused and records kept manually as of 2016.

The essay's country table (the author's AI-assisted compilation) states, citing the UNDP roadmap, that as of February 2025 the system remained mostly paper-based and that the One Patient, One Record PAS/EHR was not yet standard at the point of service.

The essay's country table (the author's AI-assisted compilation) states, citing the UNDP roadmap, that as of February 2025 the One Patient, One Record PAS/EHR project was in early rollout, piloting at one regional hospital.

The essay's country table (the author's AI-assisted compilation) states, citing the UNDP roadmap, that as of February 2025 extension of One Patient, One Record to health centres, mediclinics and community centres was planned as Phase 1 and not yet done, the pilot being at one regional hospital; it gives no count of clinics.

systems.country_label: One Patient, One Record PAS/EHR project
systems.tiers: pilot at one regional hospital; extension to health centres, mediclinics and community centres planned (February 2025)
Area Health Centres, Medi-Clinics and Community Health Centres; implementation failed, hardware unused (2016)

note: Passages file; only the Mauritius clinic row bears on health. It says aggregate reporting is 'possibly' digital, which is a conjecture and gives no HMIS fact. OpenEMIS, the police CADB and civil status systems in the other rows are not health systems.
